answers.explanation: That's the opening idea of the chapter: an execution environment plus services.
It matters when many users or jobs share the machine. A lone user rarely thinks about it.
File handling is something every user and program needs directly. Accounting and resource allocation serve the shared system.
System calls are the doorway into the OS. Nothing below that layer is called directly.
Those are the three interface styles. The next lessons cover them.
When resources are shared, someone has to make sure processes and users can't interfere with each other.
Accounting tracks who uses how much. It serves the system and its administrators, not the user's own work.
